questions.stem: What does the man say he did before buying the blender?
questions.stemZh: 男士说他在购买搅拌机之前做了什么？
questions.answerText: Read numerous comments users put online.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I did thorough research on which specific model to get. I read through maybe hundreds of online user reviews. 我对具体该买哪个型号做了彻底的研究。我大概读了几百条网上的用户评论。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 男方自述买前动作。这题问"the man...did before buying"，信号就是男方在介绍这台机器 时，自己说出的那串"我做了……"。关键落点是 I read through maybe hundreds of online user reviews，"读了几百条网上用户评论"正是买前的准备动作。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: read through maybe hundreds of online user reviews ↔ Read numerous comments users put online. 几百条=numerous，评论=comments

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: C) 原词陷阱 录音里 state-of-the-art 是男方用来夸"这台机器很先进"（this one is state-of-the- art），并不是说他"去搜寻顶配机型"。选项 Searched for the state-of-the-art models of blenders. 把这个原词搬过来拼成一个他没做的动作，听到 state-of-the-art 就选就中招。 借用原文：this one is state-of-the-art D) 偷换概念 男方确实说了 I did thorough research，但研究的是 which specific model to get（该买 哪个型号），不是价格。选项 Did thorough research on the price of kitchen appliances. 偷偷把研究对象换成 price，听到"thorough research"就选就被偷换。 借用原文：I did thorough research on which specific model to get B) 与原文相反 选项 Blended all his food without using a machine. 说"不用机器就把食物搅了"，可整段 重点恰恰是他买了一台机器（blender 就是机器）。这和录音说的正相反，属无中生有又反 向的陷阱。

analysis.text: I make a fresh fruit juice in the morning, maybe not every morning, but three or four times a week, and it feels fantastic. It's a really healthy habit. 我早上会榨一杯鲜果汁，也许不是每天早上，而是一周三四次，感觉棒极了。这是个真正健 康的习惯。

questions.stem: What do we learn about store-bought juice from the conversation?
questions.stemZh: 从对话中我们了解到关于商店购买的果汁的什么信息？

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Did you know that store-bought juice is like 10% sugar? 你知道店里买的果汁差不多有百分之十是糖吗？

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 对象store-bought juice配数字。题干对象 store-bought juice 在录音里只在 store- bought juice is like 10% sugar 这一句被正面描述，且带一个具体比例 10%。"对象点名 + 出现数字"双重信号，这句就是答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: store-bought juice is like 10% sugar ↔One-tenth of it is sugar. 10%=One-tenth

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: D) 偷换概念 It contains an assortment of nutrients. 借的 assortment of nutrients 是男方夸"自榨晨 间果汁"的（a far wider assortment of nutrients），对象是自榨果汁，不是店买果汁。题 干问的是 store-bought，对象被偷换。 借用原文：a far wider assortment of nutrients C) 原词陷阱 One's fancy may be tickled by it. 盗用 tickles my fancy，但录音里这词形容的是男方往 自榨果汁里加 anything that tickles my fancy，和店买果汁无关，是张冠李戴的原词陷 阱。 借用原文：anything that tickles my fancy B) 与原文相反 It looks healthy and attractive. 蹭了 healthy 一词，但录音说"自榨"比店买更健康（It's so much healthier），从没说"店买果汁看起来健康诱人"，attractive 更是没提，属未提及 兼相反。 借用原文：It's so much healthier 1 W: Today we have a very interesting guest. Mr. Thomas Benjamin Grimm, the mayor of Berkton, is here to talk about his job and responsibilities overseeing this charming village. Mr. Grimm, thank you for being here. W: 今天我们有一位非常有趣的嘉宾。Thomas Benjamin Grimm 先生，Berkton 的市长，来这里谈谈他 的工作以及管理这个迷人村庄的职责。Grimm 先生，感谢您的到来。 2 M: Thank you for having me. M: 感谢邀请我来。 3 W: I'd like to start by stating the obvious. Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country, and this has happened under your watch. Just how did you achieve this? W: 我想先说一个显而易见的事实。Berkton 已经成为全国最受欢迎的旅游目的地之一，而这是在您的任 期内发生的。您究竟是如何做到这一点的？ 4 M: The achievement belongs to all the residents of Berkton. It was a shared effort where everybody pitched in for the communal good. M: 这个成就属于 Berkton 的全体居民。这是一个共同的努力，每个人都为公共利益做出了贡献。 5 W: But how did this change happen? In about 10 years, Berkton has gone from a relatively unheard- of sleepy village to a must-see destination. W: 但这种改变是如何发生的呢？大约 10 年间，Berkton 从一个相对默默无闻的沉寂村庄变成了必看的 旅游目的地。 6 M: Yes, the change has truly been remarkable. Berkton was always fortunate to be endowed with such a beautiful natural allure. The Ambury Hills above the village remain untouched by human development, and the Sonora Valley just below it is equally stunning. The transformation commenced in a town hall Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. meeting in spring 2008 over 10 years ago now, when an overwhelming majority of neighbors voted in favor of "Motion 836". This legislative proposal essentially set out to harmonize the aesthetic appearance of all the houses in Berkton. The idea was that if all the properties looked a certain way with shared design features, then a village as a whole would look more beautiful. And it worked. M: 是的，这种变化确实非常显著。Berkton 一直很幸运地拥有如此美丽的自然魅力。村庄上方的 Ambury Hills 至今未受人类开发的影响，而就在其下方的 Sonora Valley 同样令人惊叹。这场转变始于 2008 年春天的一次市政厅会议，距今已有 10 多年了，当时绝大多数居民投票支持了"836 号动议"。这 项立法提案本质上是要统一 Berkton 所有房屋的美学外观。这个想法是，如果所有房产都以某种方式呈 现共同的设计特征，那么整个村庄看起来就会更美丽。而它奏效了。 7 W: It certainly did. I'm looking now at a before-and-after photo, and the change is truly remarkable. It's hard to believe it's the same place. And how do the neighbors feel now? W: 确实如此。我现在正在看一张前后对比照片，变化真的非常显著。很难相信这是同一个地方。那么现 在居民们的感受如何？ 8 M: Great pride, I would say. M: 我想说是巨大的自豪感。 9 W: But what about the multitudes of visitors now crowding the streets? Is everyone happy about that? W: 但现在大批游客涌入街道呢？每个人都对此感到高兴吗？ 10 M: The tourists we receive are a blessing, as they have completely revitalized our local economy. Every visitor is warmly welcome. M: 我们接待的游客是一种福气，因为他们彻底振兴了我们的本地经济。每一位游客都受到热烈欢迎。

questions.answerText: How he has led people of Berkton to change the village radically.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country, and this has happened under your watch. Just how did you achieve this? Berkton 已成为全国最受欢迎的旅游目的地之一，而这一切就发生在你的任期之内。你究竟 是怎么做到这一点的呢？

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 主持人在介绍后抛出的直接提问句。答案句的信号是主持人(W)在开场介绍之后说出的那句 直接发问 Just how did you achieve this?——"this" 回指上一句 "Berkton 变成热门旅游 地"，所以她问的正是 "你如何促成了这场转变"。对话题里，主持人 "介绍之后的第一个问 句" 就是答案落点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: how did you achieve this ↔How he has led people of Berkton to change the village radically this＝把村子变旅游地，即 "彻底改变村庄" this has happened under your watch ↔he has led people of Berkton "在你任期内发生"＝市长带领大家做成

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 A 用了原文反复出现的 popular as the mayor of Berkton 这些原词，但主持人问的是 "如 何改变村子"，不是 "市长本人如何变得受欢迎"；原文 popular tourist destinations 说的 是 "村子" 受欢迎，A 偷换成 "市长" 受欢迎，听到 popular 就选会中招。 借用原文：Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country B) 张冠李戴 B 说的是 the residents will turn Berkton into a tourist attraction，主语是居民、且是 "将要" 做的将来事；可主持人问的是 "你(市长)如何做到了已经发生的转变"，B 张冠李戴(把 焦点从市长换成居民)又错了时态。 借用原文：The achievement belongs to all the residents of Berkton. C) 原词陷阱 C 说 How charming he himself considers the village of Berkton to be，借用了原文 this charming village 里的 charming 一词；但 charming 是主持人介绍时用的，且主持 人问的是 "如何做到转变"，不是 "市长觉得村子多迷人"，C 把客观描述偷换成 "市长的主观 评价"。 借用原文：overseeing this charming village

questions.stemZh: 关于10年前的Berkton我们了解到什么?
questions.answerText: It was relatively unknown to the outside.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: In about 10 years, Berkton has gone from a relatively unheard-of sleepy village to a must- see destination. 大约 10 年间，Berkton 从一个相对默默无闻的沉睡小村，变成了一个必看的旅游胜地。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: "from…to…" 中 from 后即 10 年前的状态。答案信号是主持人这句 gone from a relatively unheard-of sleepy village to a must-see destination 里的 "from…to…" 结 构：from 后面 a relatively unheard-of sleepy village 正是 "10 年前" 的起点状态，to 后 面才是现在。问 "10 年前"，答案就在 from 之后。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: a relatively unheard-of sleepy village ↔It was relatively unknown to the outside unheard-of＝unknown，同义替换

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 A 说 developed only to a limited extent(只在有限程度上被开发)，但原文只说村子 "没名 气/沉睡"，从没说它 "被开发到有限程度"；这是凭 "沉睡村" 的印象自行脑补的开发说法， 原文无据。 B) 原词陷阱 B 用了原文原词 sleepy village，但把 relatively unheard-of(相对没名气)夸大成 totally isolated(完全孤立)；relatively(相对)被偷换成 totally(完全)，程度被拔高，与原文不符。 借用原文：a relatively unheard-of sleepy village D) 原词陷阱 D 说 endowed with rare natural resources，借用了原文 endowed with such a beautiful natural allure 的 endowed 与 natural；但原文说的是 "自然之美(allure)" 而非 "罕见资源(resources)"，且这句讲的不是 "10 年前的状态"，与题问的时间也不对。 借用原文：Berkton was always fortunate to be endowed with such a beautiful natural allure.

questions.stem: What resulted from the passing of the legislative proposal "Motion 836"?
questions.stemZh: 立法提案"836号动议"的通过产生了什么结果?
questions.answerText: All the houses in Berkton looked aesthetically similar.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: This legislative proposal essentially set out to harmonize the aesthetic appearance of all the houses in Berkton. The idea was that if all the properties looked a certain way with shared design features, then a village as a whole would look more beautiful. And it worked. 这项立法提案本质上是要统一 Berkton 所有房屋的外观审美。其设想是：如果所有房产都按 某种方式、带着共同的设计特征呈现，那么整个村庄看起来会更美。而它奏效了。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 提案后紧跟的 "统一外观"＋"奏效了"。答案信号有两处：一是紧跟提案的目的句 harmonize the aesthetic appearance of all the houses(统一所有房子的外观)，二是收尾 的 And it worked.(它奏效了)——"奏效" 确认了这个 "外观统一" 的效果真的实现了，正是 提案带来的结果。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: harmonize the aesthetic appearance of all the houses in Berkton ↔ All the houses in Berkton looked aesthetically similar "统一外观"＝"外观看起来相似" shared design features ↔aesthetically similar "共同设计特征"＝外观相似

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 A 说 designed by the same architect，借用了原文 shared design features 里的 design；但原文说的是 "共同的设计特征"，从没说 "出自同一个建筑师"，A 把 "设计相似" 偷换成 "同一人设计"，是听到 design 就选的陷阱。 借用原文：if all the properties looked a certain way with shared design features B) 偷换概念 B 说 lived in harmony with their neighbours(邻里和睦相处)，疑似借了原文 harmonize(统一)与 an overwhelming majority of neighbors voted 里 neighbors 的影 子；但原文是说邻居们 "投票通过提案"，harmonize 指 "统一房屋外观" 而非 "邻里关系和 睦"，B 偷换了概念。 借用原文：an overwhelming majority of neighbors voted in favor of "Motion 836" C) 未提及 C 说 enjoyed cosy housing conditions(享受舒适的居住条件)，但原文谈的是房子 "外观 是否统一、村子是否更美"，从没谈居民住得舒不舒适；cosy(舒适)是凭 "漂亮房子" 联想出 来的，原文无据。

questions.stem: Why does the man say the tourists are a blessing to Berkton?
questions.stemZh: 为什么这位男士说游客是Berkton的福音?
questions.answerText: They have helped boost the local economy.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: The tourists we receive are a blessing, as they have completely revitalized our local economy. 我们接待的游客是一种福气，因为他们彻底重振了我们当地的经济。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 因果词 as 之后即原因。答案信号是因果连词 as：它前面是判断 The tourists we receive are a blessing，后面 they have completely revitalized our local economy 才是 "为什 么是福气" 的真正原因。问 Why，答案就在 as 引出的从句里。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: they have completely revitalized our local economy ↔ They have helped boost the local economy revitalize＝boost，同义替换

questions.stem: What has the speaker discovered after a year of tough scientific study?

questions.answerText: Being forced to rise early differs from being an early bird.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: After a year of tough scientific study, however, I have discovered being forced to get up early in the morning is very different from being an early bird. 然而，经过一年艰苦的科学研究，我发现被迫早起和真正的早起者是非常不同的两回事。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 转折 however 加标记词 I have discovered。答案信号有二：however 把前文「我以为我 会被迫成为早起者」的旧假设推翻；紧跟的 I have discovered 直接挂出结论。转折后加 discovered 标记的那句就是答案句。

analysis.label: 替换

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 It is in fact quite possible to nurture a passion for sleep. 拼用了原文的 passion（a great passion），但原文 passion 指「她对睡眠本就有热情」，从未说「可以去培养」， 更不是这次研究的发现，属无中生有。 借用原文：for which I still have a great passion B) 原词陷阱 Babies can severely disrupt their parents' sleep patterns. 几乎照搬原文 having a baby has severely disrupted my sleep（disrupt 原词复现），但那是第3段交代的「为什么做 研究」，而题问「研究后发现了什么」，时间、逻辑位置都错，答非所问。 借用原文：having a baby has severely disrupted my sleep D) 与原文相反 New parents are forced to jump out of bed at the crack of dawn. 盗用 jump out of bed at the crack of dawn，但原文这是她 I assumed I'd be forced to become 的旧假 设，紧接着 however 就把它否定了，取它等于选了被推翻的内容。 借用原文：I assumed I'd be forced to become one of those people who jump out of bed at the crack of dawn Section C 1 If you read an article about a controversial issue, do you think you'd realise if it had changed your beliefs? No one knows your own mind like you do—it seems obvious that you would know if your beliefs had shifted. And yet a new paper in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggests that we actually have very poor awareness of our own belief change, meaning that we will tend to underestimate how much we've been swayed by a convincing article. 如果你读到一篇关于争议性问题的文章,你认为你会意识到它改变了你的信念吗?没有人比你自己更了解你 的想法——你会知道自己的信念是否发生了转变,这似乎是显而易见的。然而《实验心理学季刊》上的一 篇新论文表明,我们实际上对自己信念的改变认知很差,这意味着我们往往会低估自己被一篇有说服力的文 章影响的程度。 2 The researchers recruited over two hundred undergraduates across two studies and focused on their beliefs about whether physical punishment of kids is an effective form of discipline. The students reported their initial beliefs about whether physical punishment is an effective way to discipline a child on a scale from "1" completely disbelieve to "9" completely believe. Several weeks later they were given one of two research-based texts to read: each was several pages long and either presented the arguments and data in favour of physical punishment or against it. After this, the students answered some questions Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. to test their comprehension and memory of the text. Then, the students again scored their belief about whether physical punishment is effective or not. Finally, the researchers asked them to recall what their belief had been at the start of the study. 研究人员在两项研究中招募了两百多名本科生,重点关注他们对体罚儿童是否是一种有效管教形式的信念。 学生们报告了他们最初关于体罚是否是管教儿童的有效方式的信念,评分范围从"1"完全不相信到"9"完全相 信。几周后,他们被给予两篇基于研究的文本中的一篇来阅读:每篇都有几页长,要么呈现支持体罚的论据和 数据,要么呈现反对体罚的论据和数据。此后,学生们回答了一些问题以测试他们对文本的理解和记忆。然 后,学生们再次对他们关于体罚是否有效的信念进行评分。最后,研究人员要求他们回忆研究开始时他们的 信念是什么。 3 The students' belief about physical punishment changed when they read a text that argued against their own initial position. Crucially, the memory of their initial belief was shifted in the direction of their new belief—in fact, their memory was closer to their current belief than their original belief. The more their belief had changed, the larger this memory bias tended to be, suggesting the students were relying on their current belief to deduce the initial belief. The memory bias was unrelated to the measures of how well they'd understood or recalled the text, suggesting these factors didn't play a role in memory of initial belief or awareness of belief change. 当学生们阅读与他们自己最初立场相反的文本时,他们对体罚的信念发生了改变。至关重要的是,他们对最 初信念的记忆朝着新信念的方向发生了偏移——事实上,他们的记忆更接近他们当前的信念而不是最初的 信念。他们的信念改变得越多,这种记忆偏差往往就越大,这表明学生们依靠当前的信念来推断最初的信 念。记忆偏差与衡量他们对文本理解或回忆程度的指标无关,这表明这些因素在最初信念的记忆或对信念改 变的认知中没有发挥作用。 4 The researchers concede that this research was about changes to mostly moderate beliefs—it's likely the findings would be different in the context of changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs. However, our beliefs on most topics are in the moderate range, and as we go about our daily lives reading informative material, these intriguing findings suggest we are mostly ignorant of how what we just read has updated and altered our own position. 研究人员承认,这项研究是关于大多数温和信念的改变——在极端或根深蒂固的信念改变的背景下,研究结 果可能会有所不同。然而,我们对大多数话题的信念都处于温和范围内,当我们在日常生活中阅读信息性材 料时,这些有趣的发现表明我们大多不知道刚刚读到的内容如何更新和改变了我们自己的立场。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: This is certainly an example of how scientific findings can be misleading or misinterpreted over time. But it's also a great example of how scientific research should continually reexamine and question findings to get closer to the ground truth of understanding what's actually happening. 这无疑是一个例子，说明科学发现如何会随时间被误导或误读。但它也是一个绝佳的例子， 说明科学研究应当不断重新审视、质疑已有结论，以更接近事情真相的理解。

式。主从句时间对比(过去完成时与一般现在时)体现了真题中常见的时态转换。从句中的承前省略 在口语和书面语中都很典型。整体句式具有较好的代表性和迁移价值 I make a fresh fruit juice in the morning, maybe not every morning, but three or four times a week, and it feels fantastic. analysis.label: 判型

analysis.text: 主干 What does the author say about news broadcasts in America。结构平铺直叙，无 陷阱。

analysis.label: 定位

questions.stem: What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general 中明确出现 infer， 是典型推断信号。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 主干 What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general。in general 提示答案不应是局部小结论，而是适用于该群体的整体性推断。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs. 有趣的是，当按党派分组时，这种效应在共和党人中显著、而在民主党人中不显著，这意味 着真人秀里隐含的信息可能契合了人们既有的社会经济观念。 49. What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general? A) They believe strongly in the American Dream. B) They strive to climb the socio-economic ladder. C) They have a very strong affiliation with their party. D) They tend to watch more rags-to-riches TV shows.

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) ✓ 正确 this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats ↔ believe strongly in the American Dream play into people’s existing socioeconomic beliefs ↔believe strongly in the American Dream 预判结论是『共和党人本就更信美国梦』，选项 A 是这一推断的标准表达。 B) 无中生有 原文只比较了党派对美国梦的信念差异，从未提到任一党派的人在 socio-economic ladder 上的实际行动。 C) 偷换概念 when participants were separated by party affiliation 中 party affiliation 只是『按 党派分组』的研究操作变量，并未评价共和党人对自己政党的归属感强弱。 D) 过度推断 原文只说看了 rags-to-riches 短片后，对美国梦信仰加深的效应在共和党人中显著；并 未说共和党人比民主党人更常或更多地观看此类节目。 关于相信向上流动的人,文中陈述了什么? A) 他们可能会因自己的困境而责怪政府。 B) 他们认为政治后果绝非微不足道。 C) 他们尊重努力攀登社会阶梯的个人。 D) 他们不太可能赞成对抗不平等的政策。

questions.stem: What is stated about people who believe in upward mobility?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What is stated about people who believe in upward mobility 用 stated 询问对该人群 所作的陈述，是细节题。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 主干 What is stated about people…？被动语态，who believe in upward mobility 是 people 的定语从句，提示要找作者直接说明这类人会怎样的句子。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality. 问题就在这里：如果人们错误地以为只要努力工作就足以让个人过上更好的生活，他们就可 能更不支持那些其实能对抗不平等的政策。 50. What is stated about people who believe in upward mobility? A) They are likely to blame the government for their plight. B) They regard political consequences as anything but trivial. C) They respect individuals striving to climb the social ladder. D) They are less likely to approve of policies to fight inequality.

analysis.label: 选项

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about one's loss of a job?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What do we learn from the passage about one's loss of a job? 指向一个具体事实—— 失业会带来什么——并未问推断或主旨。 51. What do we learn from the passage about one's loss of a job? A) It compels them to visit a clinical psychologist. B) It offers them a chance to play different roles. C) It renders them puzzled about who they are. D) It forces them to redefine their life's goals.

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 主干 What do we learn from the passage 中 we 是主语、learn 是谓语；about one's loss of a job 是 learn 的范围介词短语，指明问的对象是「失去工作这件事」。句式平铺直 叙，无陷阱。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: "Without my job I don't know who I am," is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair. Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself. 「没有了工作，我就不知道自己是谁」——这话在我办公室的椅子上不止一次被来访者说 出。事实上，与那些失去或被迫更换工作的来访者一起处理这种感受，是我工作中最具挑战 的部分之一。这种失落所引发的身份危机，要远远大于失业本身。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 偷换概念 原文只是说作者本人是 clinical psychologist 处理来访者的身份危机，并未要求 visit a clinical psychologist；A 把作者视角偷换成失业者的行为。 B) 张冠李戴 原文段 2 并未说失业「提供了扮演不同角色的机会」；段 3 才谈多重身份，但与「失业 带来什么」是两个话题。 C) ✓ 正确 Without my job I don't know who I am ↔puzzled about who they are This loss provokes an identity crisis ↔It renders them puzzled 预判的「不知道自己是谁」与 It renders them puzzled about who they are 在主语、 谓语致使关系、宾语状态上完全对应，确定 C。 D) 过度推断 原文谈的是 identity crisis 与重新审视自我信念，并没有说失业必然要 redefine their life's goals，把身份层面的事推到了「人生目标」的宏大命题上。 作者对我们的身份认同有了什么理解? A) 它对我们的情感健康至关重要。 B) 它在生活的许多方面发挥重要作用。 C) 它反映了我们在社会中不断变化的地位。 D) 它比表面看起来更复杂。

options.label: A
options.text: It compels them to visit a clinical psychologist.

options.label: B
options.text: It offers them a chance to play different roles.

options.label: C
options.text: It renders them puzzled about who they are.

options.label: D
options.text: It forces them to redefine their life's goals.

questions.stem: What has the author come to understand about our identity?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What has the author come to understand about our identity? 指向原文一句明确表 述，不要求跨段推理。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 完成时 What has the author come to understand 用 has come to understand 强调认 知过程已完成；about our identity 指明认知对象。结构简单。 52. What has the author come to understand about our identity? A) It is crucial to our emotional wellbeing. B) It plays a big role in many facets of life. C) It reflects our changing status in society. D) It is more complicated than it appears.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance. 然而，我逐渐明白的一件事是：我们的身份远比乍看之下复杂得多。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 偷换概念 原文段 3 后半句说 my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing，主语是「适应身份的能力」，并非身份本身；A 把「能力对 幸福重要」偷换成「身份对情绪幸福重要」。 B) 答非所问 原文确实列了多种身份角色，但作者「come to understand」的核心是「身份复杂」这 一判断，而非「身份在生活方方面面起作用」；B 只描述现象，未答出认知本身。 C) 过度推断 原文 They change over time 谈的是「我们在不同时期的身份变化」（学生、毕业生、 咨询师等），并非社会地位的变化；C 偷偷加上了 status in society。 D) ✓ 正确 much more complex than we recognise at first glance ↔more complicated than it appears 预判要点「复杂」「超出表面认知」两块在 more complicated than it appears 里一一 落地，无遗漏，确定 D。 文章关于我们在工作中的身份认同说了什么? A) 它们对我们的自尊至关重要。 B) 它们随着时间的推移而演变。 C) 它们凌驾于所有其他自我认知之上。 D) 它们是理解我们自己的关键。

options.label: A
options.text: It is crucial to our emotional wellbeing.

options.label: B
options.text: It plays a big role in many facets of life.

options.label: C
options.text: It reflects our changing status in society.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about our identities at work?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What does the passage say about our identities at work? 让考生回原文找关于「职场 身份」的明示句。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What does the passage say about our identities at work：say 是谓语、about 引出宾 语对象；our identities at work 中 at work 修饰 identities，限定「工作中的」身份。无 难点。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time. 此外，我们在工作中的身份并非一成不变。它们会随时间而变化。 53. What does the passage say about our identities at work? A) They are essential to our self-esteem. B) They evolve with the passage of time. C) They overrule all other self-perceptions. D) They are key to understanding ourselves.

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 无中生有 原文谈的是 wellbeing、identity crisis，没有 self-esteem（自尊）的概念，A 属于原 文未提的新信息。 B) ✓ 正确 They change over time ↔They evolve with the passage of time 预判「随时间而变」直接命中 They evolve with the passage of time，主谓宾全对 应，定 B。 C) 与原文相反 段 3 强调的是身份的「多元」与「变化」，并未说工作身份压倒其他身份；恰相反，作 者承认我们还可作为朋友、配偶等存在。 D) 答非所问 「身份是理解自己的关键」与 Q52 的「身份很复杂」更接近，但题问的是 our identities at work 的具体属性；D 没有答出「随时间而变」这一具体属性。 在当今不断变化的就业市场中我们必须做什么? A) 努力发展我们的社会身份。 B) 为不同的职业道路做准备。 C) 始终努力保持自信果断。 D) 学会管理不确定性。

options.label: A
options.text: They are essential to our self-esteem.

options.label: B
options.text: They evolve with the passage of time.

options.label: D
options.text: They are key to understanding ourselves.

questions.stem: What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market? 指向原文一句给出具体 动作的陈述。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market?：do 是询问的动作；in 引导的状语 in today's ever-changing job market 限定背景。句式直白。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market. 尽管我们倾向于消除生活中的不确定性，但在某种程度上我们必须学会管理不确定性，尤其 是在如今这个动荡多变的就业市场中。 54. What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market? A) Strive to develop our social identity. B) Prepare for different career paths. C) Try to be assertive at all times. D) Learn to manage uncertainty.

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 偷换概念 原文谈 career identity / our identities at work，从未出现 social identity；A 凭空替 换了限定语。 B) 张冠李戴 「为不同职业路径做准备」更接近段 4 的 career progression / new sectors，但 Q54 问的是动荡市场下「必须做的事」，原文给的明确答案是 manage uncertainty。 C) 以偏概全 原文只是举例说有人在职场会变得 assertive，并未要求所有人 at all times 都要果断； C 把范围扩到全部场景，与原文不符。 D) ✓ 正确 we have to manage uncertainty ↔Learn to manage uncertainty predict 的「学会管理不确定性」与 Learn to manage uncertainty 字面几乎一致，确 定 D。 为了拓展职业选择我们应该做什么? A) 改变我们对自己的认知。 B) 比较各种工作机会。 C) 关注新兴行业领域。 D) 有意识地进行自我约束。

options.label: A
options.text: Strive to develop our social identity.

options.label: C
options.text: Try to be assertive at all times.

questions.stem: What should we do to expand our career options?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What should we do to expand our career options? 求一个明确的应对动作。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What should we do to expand our career options?：should we do 是主干，to expand our career options 是目的状语，说明动作要服务的目标。结构平铺直叙。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options. 在一个职业发展可能把我们带入新行业的时代，挑战我们对自我的认知、并探索是否能通 过改变你对自己持有的信念来创造一种新的身份体验、以拓宽你的职业选择，变得越来越 重要。 55. What should we do to expand our career options? A) Alter our perceptions of ourselves. B) Compare various job opportunities. C) Look into newly emerging sectors. D) Exercise self-discipline consciously.

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) ✓ 正确 changing the beliefs you hold about yourself ↔Alter our perceptions of ourselves challenge our sense of self ↔Alter our perceptions of ourselves 预判要点「改变自我信念」在 Alter our perceptions of ourselves 中以同义改写完整呈 现，确定 A。 B) 无中生有 原文谈的是「改变信念以扩展选择」，并非 Compare various job opportunities；B 把心理层面的动作偷换为外部信息搜集行为。 C) 答非所问 原文 career progression may lead us into new sectors 只是时代背景描述，作者并未 让读者去 Look into newly emerging sectors。 D) 以偏概全 原文 through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline 只是改变信 念的途径之一；题干问的是「为扩展职业选择」最直接该做的事，作者明确给出的是改 变信念，而非单独突出自律。

P1 The "American Dream" promises that in the Land of Opportunity, any individual can climb the economic ladder and prosper through hard work and ambition alone. And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations.

P2 So why does the idea of the American Dream persist? A new study in the American Journal of Political Science identifies one factor that has been overlooked: the influence of reality TV.

P3 Reality shows have come to dominate US television over the past 20 years, notes Eunji Kim from Vanderbilt University. And the overwhelming majority of these have a "rags-to-riches" storyline: they feature ordinary Americans who work hard to achieve great economic success. And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts—which paint a more realistic Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage. view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans—get a much smaller proportion of the viewership.

P4 Rags-to-riches stories are ubiquitous(无处不在的) on TV—but does watching these programmes actually convince people that economic mobility is easily attainable? To find out, Kim's team had participants watch a 5-minute clip from a reality show with a rags-to-riches storyline. Control participants watched a clip from a reality show that didn't have a rags-to-riches story. After watching the shows, participants rated how much they agreed with four statements relating to the American Dream.

P5 The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream. Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs.

P6 Kim also conducted a survey of 3,000 US residents. They also rated the extent to which they believed success in life is related to various internal factors (such as ambition) and external factors (such as family wealth). Finally, they read a list of TV programmes and indicated which they regularly watched.

P7 Participants who were heavy viewers of rags-to-riches programmes or frequent viewers had a stronger belief in the American Dream than those who never watched such shows.

P8 Kim concludes that "rags-to-riches entertainment media are an important cultural force that promotes and perpetuates beliefs in upward mobility". And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality.

P9 "In this era of choice, entertainment media is what captures hearts and minds," Kim writes. "Its political consequences are anything but trivial".

P1 When someone asks us 'what do you do?' we nearly always reply with our occupation. Work, for many of us, is much more than a job. It is the defining aspect of our identity. For many of us it is through our job that we can define ourselves.

P2 "Without my job I don't know who I am," is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair. Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself.

P3 One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance. If we take the time to reflect we might recognise that as well as our work we can also identify as a friend, a spouse, a son or daughter, a parent, a member of a sports team or religious community. We may recognise that we feel and act differently in these roles and relationships than we do at work. The passive daughter becomes an assertive leader at work. Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time. I myself have been a shop Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage. assistant, a waitress, a student, a graduate, and a clinical psychologist. At each stage my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing. Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market.

P4 How we see ourselves is central to the issue of our identity. When we tell ourselves "I'm good at starting projects but not so great at seeing them through" it can become part of our belief system. But if you have the unfortunate experience of an enforced job change you will need to examine those beliefs to see how grounded in reality they are. You will be required to ask yourself how helpful these beliefs are and consider personal change. We can change our beliefs, behaviours and emotional experience at any time through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline. In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options. Ultimately it is you who define who you are. You are only your job if you let it be so.

translation.reference: China abounds in bamboo and is among the first countries to develop and utilize bamboo resources. Bamboo is widely distributed across China and comes in a rich variety of species. It is also highly practical and is used in many aspects of production and daily life, such as making chopsticks, tables and chairs, and building bridges and houses. The Chinese people love bamboo, and since ancient times countless scholars have created splendid literary and artistic works with bamboo as their theme. The straight stem of bamboo symbolizes an upright character. Moreover, bamboo has strong vitality and adaptability; no matter how harsh the environment is, it can survive tenaciously, thus symbolizing the spirit of perseverance. For thousands of years, bamboo has been regarded as a symbol of the character of the Chinese nation.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: China 作主语，abounds / is 作两个谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 中文 中国盛产竹子，是最早开发利用竹资源的国家 两个分句共用同一个主语"中国"，所以英文主 语就用 China。前半句核心动词"盛产"译 abounds in / is rich in；后半句"是……国家"用系动词 is + 表语 the country。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: "最早开发利用竹资源的"降级成定语从句修饰 country 最早开发利用竹资源的国家 里"最早开发利用竹资源"是用来修饰"国家"的一长串定语，照中文塞在 country 前面会很别扭，应降级成后置定语从句 the first country to develop and utilize bamboo resources（用不定式作定语）或 that was among the first to use bamboo resources，挂到 country 后面。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调，用一般现在时：China abounds in bamboo and is the first country…，陈述长 期事实。 搭配 "盛产"用 abound in 或 be rich in；abound 是不及物动词，必须接介词 in，写成 China abounds in bamboo，不能说 abounds bamboo。 单复数 bamboo 作植物总称不可数，用单数；"竹资源"含多种资源用复数 bamboo resources。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: China abounds in bamboo and is among the first countries to develop and utilize bamboo resources. 2. 竹子在中国分布广泛，品种丰富。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: Bamboo 作主语，is 系动词带两个并列表语（主语策略：原句主语） 竹子在中国分布广泛，品种丰富 两个分句都在描述竹子的状态，主语都是"竹子"，用 Bamboo 作 主语；"分布广泛"译 is widely distributed，"品种丰富"译 comes in rich varieties / has a great variety of species。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 两个并列描述用 with 或 and 合成一句 "分布广泛"和"品种丰富"是对竹子的两点并列描述，可处理成 Bamboo is widely distributed in China and comes in a rich variety of species；也可把后半句降级成 with 介词短语：Bamboo is widely distributed across China, with a rich variety of species，避免两个短句平铺。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 长期事实，沿用一般现在时 is / comes。 语态 "分布"在英文里习惯用被动 is distributed（竹子是被分布的对象），符合英语被动多于汉语的特 点。 单复数 varieties / species 表"多个品种"用复数；bamboo 仍作不可数单数，谓语 is、comes 用第三人称 单数。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Bamboo is widely distributed across China and comes in a rich variety of species. 3. 竹子实用性强，用于生产和生活的许多方面，如筷子、桌椅的制作和桥梁、房屋的建造。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: Bamboo 作主语，is 系动词带 highly practical（主语策略：原句主语） 竹子实用性强 是全句主干，主语"竹子"译 Bamboo，"实用性强"用系表 is highly practical / is very useful。后面"用于……""如……"都是对实用性的展开说明。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: "用于"降级成被动分词，"如"举例用 such as 引出 用于生产和生活的许多方面 降级成过去分词短语 used in many aspects of production and daily life 作后置定语或状语；如筷子、桌椅的制作和桥梁、房屋的建造 用 such as 引出并列名词短语： such as making chopsticks, tables and chairs, and building bridges and houses，把中 文"……的制作/建造"转成动名词 making / building。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 沿用一般现在时 is、is used，陈述竹子的常态用途。 语态 "用于"用被动 is used in（竹子被用于），承受动作的竹子作主语，符合英语习惯。 单复数 chopsticks 只有复数形式；tables and chairs、bridges and houses 泛指此类物品均用复数。 并列一致 such as 后并列的两组用 and 连接、结构对称：making chopsticks… and building bridges…， 动名词形式保持一致。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Bamboo is highly practical and is used in many aspects of production and daily life, such as making chopsticks, tables and chairs, and building bridges and houses. 4. 中国人爱竹，自古以来就有无数文人以竹为主题，创作了绚丽多彩的文学和绘画作品。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 前半 The Chinese love bamboo；后半 countless scholars 作主语带 have created（主语策 略：原句主语） 本句含两套主语：中国人爱竹 主语是"中国人"译 The Chinese，谓语 love；自古以来就有无数文 人……创作了……作品 主语换成"无数文人"译 countless scholars / men of letters，核心谓语"创 作了"译 have created。两套主语分别立主干，用分号或 and 连接。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: "以竹为主题"降级成介词短语，"自古以来"作时间状语 以竹为主题 降级成介词短语 with bamboo as their theme / on the theme of bamboo 作状 语，修饰"创作"；自古以来 译时间状语 since ancient times，因其表"从过去延续至今"，触发后半 句用现在完成时 have created。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 "中国人爱竹"是恒常事实用一般现在时 love；"自古以来……创作了……"由 since ancient times 触 发现在完成时 have created（动作从古延续到今、影响仍在），这是本句对全篇基调的合理偏离。 主谓一致 The Chinese 表"中国人"这一群体作复数，谓语用 love（非 loves）；countless scholars 复数， 谓语 have created。 物主代词 "以竹为主题"中"主题"属文人，用 their theme，与主语 scholars 保持一致。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The Chinese people love bamboo, and since ancient times countless scholars have created splendid literary and artistic works with bamboo as their theme. 5. 竹子主干(stem) 笔直，象征正直的品格。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: The stem of bamboo 作主语，is straight 作谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 竹子主干(stem) 笔直 主语是"竹子主干"译 The stem of bamboo / Its straight stem，谓语"笔 直"用系表 is straight；象征正直的品格 的"象征"译 symbolizes。原文已给提示词 stem，直接 采用。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: "笔直"与"象征"可合成主干+伴随，或并列两动作 两个分句可处理成 The stem of bamboo is straight, symbolizing an upright character（把"象 征"降为 -ing 分词作结果状语），或并列 The straight stem of bamboo symbolizes an upright character（把"笔直"提为定语、"象征"作谓语）。后者更凝练，避免两个短句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 沿用一般现在时 is / symbolizes，陈述竹子的恒常象征义。 主谓一致 主语 The stem（单数）或 The straight stem，谓语用第三人称单数 is / symbolizes（带 -s）。 冠词与用词 "正直的品格"译 an upright character / integrity；character 表抽象品格时用单数，前加不定冠 词 an upright character。"正直"用 upright / honest，不宜用 straight（straight 指物理笔 直）。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The straight stem of bamboo symbolizes an upright character. 6. 竹子具有强大的生命力和适应能力，无论环境多么恶劣，都能够顽强生存，因而寓意坚韧不 拔的精神。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: Bamboo 作主语，has 作核心谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 竹子具有强大的生命力和适应能力 是主干，主语"竹子"译 Bamboo，谓语"具有"译 has，宾语 strong vitality and adaptability。后面"无论环境多么恶劣，都能顽强生存""因而寓意……"是让步 与结果的展开。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: "无论……恶劣"作让步状语，"因而寓意"用分词或 thus 引出结果 无论环境多么恶劣，都能够顽强生存 译成 no matter how harsh the environment is, it can survive tenaciously，作让步状语从句；因而寓意坚韧不拔的精神 用 thus symbolizing the spirit of perseverance（-ing 分词作结果状语）或 and therefore symbolizes…，显出"因而"的因果。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 全句陈述竹子常态，沿用一般现在时 has、can survive、symbolizes。 让步从句语序 no matter how harsh the environment is 用陈述语序（how + 形容词 + 主语 + is），不要写成 疑问语序 how harsh is the environment。 不可数名词 vitality（生命力）、adaptability（适应能力）、perseverance（坚韧不拔）均为抽象不可数名 词，不加复数、一般不加冠词。 用词 "恶劣"用 harsh / adverse 修饰 environment；"顽强"用 tenaciously / stubbornly。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Bamboo has strong vitality and adaptability; no matter how harsh the environment is, it can survive tenaciously, thus symbolizing the spirit of perseverance. 7. 几千年来，竹子一直被视为中华民族品格的象征。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: Bamboo 作主语，has been regarded as 被动谓语（主语策略：转被动） 竹子一直被视为中华民族品格的象征 中文已用"被"字，直接对应英文被动：主语 Bamboo（承 受"视为"动作的对象），谓语 has been regarded as / has been seen as，表语 a symbol of the character of the Chinese nation。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: "几千年来"作时间状语前置，"中华民族品格的象征"作表语 几千年来 译 For thousands of years 作时间状语，置于句首；中华民族品格的象征 处理成 a symbol of the character of the Chinese nation 作 regarded as 的表语，用 of 短语层层修饰， 避免照中文"……的……的"硬堆。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 "几千年来一直"表从过去持续至今，触发现在完成时被动 has been regarded as，是对一般现在时 基调的合理偏离，与第 4 句同理。 语态 "被视为"用被动 be regarded/seen as，符合原文"被"字。 冠词 regarded as a symbol 用不定冠词 a（泛指一种象征）；the Chinese nation 用定冠词 the（特 指中华民族）。
